newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends weaker in tandem with CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends weaker in tandem with CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on the back of weaker CBOT soybeans and commercial selling.
"We did have good two-way trade (in canola). There was very good commercial and crusher buying as well as good commercial selling and hedge pressure," one trader said.
Flax was down in sympathy with canola. "We had some trading in the October/November spread, closing at $24 a tonne which widened the inverse by 10 cents," a trader said.
Good commercial selling appeared in the February western barley contract, one analyst said. UGG was a good seller of the November/February spread at $4.50.
Traders are also watching for the September Pool Return Outlook by the Canadian Wheat Board this afternoon with trade expectations of lower numbers, the analyst said.
In feed wheat, prices were pressured by commercial selling. Cargill was a light seller of the March and December and there was good two-sided commercial trade in October feed wheat, the analyst said.

November canola lost $2.70 at $437.30 a tonne while January canola fell $3.50 at $440.10. October flax was off $0.60 at $398.00 at tonne. November western barley dropped $2.10 at $148.20 and October feed wheat fell $1.30 to $200.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for Feed Peas which are in US dollars).
